page.overview:
Who is Tar-Atanamir?

Tar-Atanamir also known as Atanamir the Great was the thirteenth King of Númenor.

Tar-Atanamir succeeded his father, King Tar-Ciryatan, in SA 2029. He was married to an unnamed woman and had a son named Tar-Ancalimon and another unnamed child that eventually led up to Herucalmo. Tar-Atanamir began to speak against the Valar in particular the Ban of the Valar and the Gift of Ilúvatar. He was also the first king who was unwilling to give up his throne voluntarily before his death, and to let himself die while he was still strong in mind and body. His reign is thus generally considered to constitute the beginning of Númenor's moral decline.

The Valar were perturbed that the Númenóreans spoke against the Ban of the Valar and sent ambassadors to Tar-Atanamir to attempt to reassure them and halt their growing fear of death. The king demanded to know why his ancestors Eärendil and Tuor lived in Valinor and had eternal life yet he did not. The ambassadors answered that theirs was a fate apart and that the Undying Lands did not themselves make their inhabitants immortal, but were named for those that dwelled in them. Tar-Atanamir was not satisfied with these answers.

He was the first king to refuse to die willingly and give up the Sceptre; death instead took him by force and thus his reign ended. Thus every ruler afterwards did not renounce their reign and accept death before dotage. Tar-Atanamir ruled for one hundred ninety-two years and was succeeded by his son, Tar-Ancalimon. After his death the lifespans of the House of Elros would begin to wane.
